close_reason: Fixed in d3adb1f: SpaceInvite has manual Debug impl that redacts code. Regression test space_invite_debug_does_not_leak_code uses a canary literal that's never derived from the code under test.
description:
Location: `crate-jmap-chat-types/src/space.rs:88-114`

  #[non_exhaustive]
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub struct SpaceInvite {
      pub id: Id,
      pub code: String,   // <-- unguessable secret per backend.rs:74-89
      ...
  }

CONCERN
`SpaceInvite.code` is the unguessable invite-code credential (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.18, ChatBackend trait doc at backend.rs:74-89). Anyone with the `code` value can join the Space — it is functionally a chat-server invite-link token.

The type derives `Debug` with no manual redaction, so any `{:?}`-format of a `SpaceInvite` value writes the credential to the output stream. Cases:

- A future `tracing::debug!("invite created: {:?}", invite)` call lands in operator logs.
- A test harness or fixture-generator that Debug-prints a SpaceInvite checks in to git.
- A `#[derive(Debug)]` consumer struct that wraps SpaceInvite (e.g. a chat-server response builder) inherits the leak.
- The current WsFrame::Unknown variant (ws/mod.rs:67-75) Debug-prints `raw: serde_json::Value` which can contain a SpaceInvite serialization.

This is exactly the shape that motivated the closed JMAP-sc1b.79 for BearerAuth/BasicAuth (manual redacting Debug impl + canary regression test). SpaceInvite is the SAME class of secret-bearing public type and got missed.

WHAT GOES WRONG
Confidentiality / key recovery — the invite-link token is leaked through any Debug-format path. Once leaked into a log or a CI artifact, the invite can be redeemed by anyone with read access to that log.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Remove `Debug` from the derive list at space.rs:90.
2. Add a manual Debug impl that redacts `code` to `"[REDACTED]"` (mirror the BearerAuth shape at auth.rs:183-189).
3. Add a regression test that constructs SpaceInvite with a canary code and asserts the canary does not appear in `{:?}` output (mirror auth.rs:443-475 test pattern added by .79).
4. Consider applying the same treatment to PushSubscriptionPatch.verification_code (separate bead).

ORACLE
- Canonical: the JMAP-sc1b.79 fix for BearerAuth/BasicAuth is the in-repo precedent.
- ChatBackend trait doc-comment at `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:74-89` defines the `code` field as a credential.
- draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.18 normatively defines SpaceInvite.code.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P2. Live confidentiality defect on a public credential-bearing type. The crate is positioned as canonical for the JMAP Chat wire format (per AGENTS.md), so any downstream consumer that imports SpaceInvite inherits the unsafe-by-default Debug derive.
title: Security: SpaceInvite derives Debug exposing the unguessable code field (crate-jmap-chat-types/src/space.rs:90)
